lede: For a month Madinah whispered about the Prophet’s wife, and no revelation came. Then ten ayat came down and cleared her by name of what was said. Around them the surah builds the laws that keep a society clean — and at its centre it hangs a lamp: “Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth.”

names.name: al-Nūr
names.note: After the ayah of Light (24:35). The word runs through the passage around it: “light upon light”, and “he to whom Allah gives no light has no light.”

revelation.detail: Ibn al-Jawzī says it is Madinan, all of it, by agreement, and al-Qurṭubī says the same and names its purpose in a line: the rulings of chastity and of covering. Its date is fixed by the event at its centre. The slander against ʿĀʾishah was spread on the return from the expedition against Banū al-Muṣṭaliq, in the fifth or sixth year after the Hijrah, and her vindication came about a month later. The traditional order places it one hundred and second.
revelation.when: Madinah, after the expedition against Banū al-Muṣṭaliq — the fifth or sixth year

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ النُّورِ وَهِيَ مَدَنيَّةٌ كُلُّها بِإجْماعِهِمْ
مَقْصُودُ هَذِهِ السُّورَةِ ذِكْرُ أَحْكَامِ الْعَفَافِ وَالسِّتْرِ

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ مَرْدُوَيْهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ النُّورِ بِالمَدِينَةِ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Madinah. Recorded by Ibn Mardawayh.

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ مَرْدَوَيْهِ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ وابْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ قالا: أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةُ النُّورِ بِالمَدِينَةِ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn al-Zubayr: it came down in Madinah. Recorded by Ibn Mardawayh.

setting: ʿĀʾishah tells it herself, in one of the longest narrations in the two Ṣaḥīḥs. On the way back from an expedition the army halted at night. She walked away from the camp, and returning found her necklace gone; she went back to look for it. The men who carried her litter lifted it onto the camel thinking she was inside — “women were light in those days” — and the army moved on. She sat down where she was and fell asleep. Ṣafwān ibn al-Muʿaṭṭal, who followed behind the army, found her at dawn, said only “To Allah we belong and to Him we return,” made his camel kneel, and led it on foot until they caught up at midday.

That was enough. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, the leader of the hypocrites, took the largest part in what was then said, and others repeated it. ʿĀʾishah fell ill on reaching Madinah and for a month knew nothing, except that she missed the Prophet’s usual gentleness. When she learned of it she went to her parents’ house and wept, she says, until she thought her liver would split. The Prophet ﷺ came and sat with her: “ʿĀʾishah, I have been told such and such about you. If you are innocent, Allah will declare your innocence.” She turned to her father, and then her mother, to answer for her, and each said: by Allah, we do not know what to say. So she answered herself, in the words of the father of Yūsuf: “Patience is beautiful, and Allah is the one whose help is sought against what you describe.”

He had not risen from where he sat when the revelation came upon him. When it lifted he was smiling, and the first thing he said was: “ʿĀʾishah — Allah has declared you innocent.” She says she had never imagined that Qurʾan would be recited about her; the most she had hoped for was that he might be shown a dream.

The rest of the surah is built outward from that month. The penalty for the one who accuses a chaste woman and cannot bring four witnesses. The rule for a husband who accuses his own wife. Ask leave before you enter a house not your own. Lower your gaze; draw the head-covering over the chest. Marry off the single among you. And then, where one would expect only more law, the surah turns to the light by which all of this is seen.

occasions.title: The slander
occasions.text: ʿĀʾishah tells it herself. On the way back from a campaign the army halted for the night near Madinah. When the order to march was given she walked out beyond the camp, and on returning found that her necklace of Ẓafār beads had broken and fallen. She went back to look for it. The men who saddled her camel lifted her litter onto it thinking she was inside — she was a young girl and weighed little — and the army moved off. She found the necklace, came back to an empty camp where there was “no one to call and no one to answer”, and sat down where she had been, sure that they would miss her and return. There she fell asleep.
story: Ṣafwān ibn al-Muʿaṭṭal was travelling behind the army. He reached the place at dawn, saw the shape of someone sleeping, and knew her, for he had seen her before the screen was prescribed. She woke to his saying, “To Allah we belong and to Him we return,” and drew her garment over her face. “By Allah, he did not speak a word to me, and I heard no word from him but that.” He made his camel kneel, she mounted, and he walked leading it until they came up with the army at its midday halt. “And then those who were to be ruined were ruined.” The one who took the greater part in the lie was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy.

In Madinah she fell ill for a month, and knew nothing of what was being said. What troubled her was only that she missed the tenderness the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had always shown her in illness: he would come in, give the greeting, ask, “How is she?” and go. She learned of it when she was recovering, from Umm Misṭaḥ, who tripped on her own cloak as they walked out at night and cursed her son. “What an evil thing to say — do you curse a man who was at Badr?” — “Have you not heard what he said?” And she told her. ʿĀʾishah’s illness doubled. She asked leave to go to her parents, to be certain of it, and her mother said: “Daughter, take it lightly. It is seldom that a beautiful woman is loved by her husband and has fellow-wives, but they find much to say about her.” She wept that whole night until morning.

The revelation delayed, and the Prophet ﷺ consulted those close to him. Usāmah ibn Zayd spoke of what he knew of her innocence: “Your wife, Messenger of Allah; we know nothing but good.” ʿAlī said: “Allah has not made things narrow for you, and there are many women besides her; and if you ask the maidservant, she will tell you the truth.” So he asked Barīrah, who said: “By Him who sent you with the truth, I have never seen anything in her to find fault with, except that she is a young girl who falls asleep over her family’s dough, and the sheep comes and eats it.” He ﷺ stood on the pulpit: “Muslims, who will relieve me of a man whose harm has reached my own household? By Allah, I know nothing of my wife but good; and they have named a man of whom I know nothing but good.” Saʿd ibn Muʿādh rose to offer it, Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah rose against him, Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr rose against Saʿd, and the Aws and the Khazraj were on the point of fighting while he ﷺ stood there, calming them until they were quiet.

She had wept two nights and a day, until her parents thought the weeping would split her liver, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in and sat down — he had not sat with her since it began. He bore witness, and said: “ʿĀʾishah, such and such has reached me about you. If you are innocent, Allah will clear you. And if you have fallen into a sin, ask Allah’s forgiveness and turn to Him; for when a servant admits his sin and repents, Allah turns to him.” Her tears stopped so that she could not feel a drop. She said to her father, “Answer the Messenger of Allah for me.” He said: “By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah.” She asked her mother, and her mother said the same.

So she answered for herself — “a young girl who had not read much of the Qurʾan”: “By Allah, I know that you have heard this story until it has settled in your hearts and you have believed it. If I tell you that I am innocent — and Allah knows that I am innocent — you will not believe me; and if I confess to you something of which Allah knows I am innocent, you will believe me. By Allah, I find no likeness for myself and you but what the father of Yūsuf said: ‘Patience is beautiful, and it is Allah whose help is sought against what you describe.’” Then she turned away and lay down on her bed. She knew that Allah would clear her; but she had never supposed that He would send down, about her, revelation that would be recited. “I was too small a thing in my own eyes for Allah to speak of me in words that are recited.” She had only hoped that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ might be shown it in a dream.

“By Allah, he had not risen from where he sat, and none of the household had gone out, before it came down upon him.” The weight of it took him as it always did, until the sweat ran from him like pearls though the day was wintry. When it lifted he was laughing, and the first thing he said was: “ʿĀʾishah — Allah has declared you innocent.” Her mother said, “Stand up and go to him.” She said: “By Allah, I will not stand up for him, and I will praise none but Allah.” Allah had sent down the ten ayat that begin, “Those who brought the lie are a band among you.”

Abū Bakr had been supporting Misṭaḥ ibn Uthāthah, who was his kinsman and poor, and he swore he would never spend on him again after what he had said. Then came down: “Let not those of bounty and means among you swear off giving to kinsmen, to the poor, and to those who emigrated in the way of Allah. Let them pardon and overlook. Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?” Abū Bakr said: “Yes, by Allah, I love that Allah should forgive me,” and he restored to Misṭaḥ what he used to give him, and said: “By Allah, I will never take it from him.” And Zaynab bint Jaḥsh — the one among the wives who rivalled ʿĀʾishah — when she was asked, said: “Messenger of Allah, I guard my hearing and my sight. I know nothing but good.”

occasions.title: The husband who accuses his wife
occasions.text: Hilāl ibn Umayyah accused his wife before the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “The proof, or the penalty on your back.” He said: “Messenger of Allah, if one of us sees a man upon his wife, is he to go looking for proof?… By Him who sent you with the truth, I am telling the truth, and Allah will surely send down what clears my back of the penalty.” And Jibrīl came down with: “Those who accuse their wives…”
occasions.source: Ibn ʿAbbās: al-Bukhārī (4747). The same is told of ʿUwaymir al-ʿAjlānī, from Sahl ibn Saʿd: al-Bukhārī (4745).

occasions.title: Marthad and ʿAnāq
occasions.text: Marthad ibn Abī Marthad used to carry Muslim captives out of Makkah to Madinah. A woman of Makkah named ʿAnāq, a prostitute, had been his companion before Islam. He asked the Prophet ﷺ: “Messenger of Allah, may I marry ʿAnāq?” He gave no answer until this ayah came down, and then said: “Do not marry her.”
occasions.source: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr: al-Tirmidhī (3177), Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasāʾī; its chain is ḥasan according to al-Albānī.

aim: To centre on chastity and covering, and on the purity of the Muslim community — fortifying it against the causes of indecency, and against the plotting of the hypocrites to spread it.
themes: The penalties for adultery and for false accusation
The promise of succession in the land

outline.title: A surah sent down and made binding
outline.summary: A surah We have sent down and made obligatory. The woman and the man who commit fornication: a hundred lashes each, and let no pity for them hold you back from the religion of Allah. Those who accuse chaste women and do not bring four witnesses: eighty lashes, and never accept their testimony again. And those who accuse their own wives, with no witness but themselves: four oaths by Allah, and a fifth invoking His curse if he lies — and she averts the penalty by the same.

outline.title: The slander
outline.summary: Those who brought the slander are a band among you. Do not think it bad for you; it is good for you. Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and women not think well of their own people, and say, “This is a plain lie”? You took it up with your tongues and thought it a light matter, while with Allah it was immense. Do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Let them pardon and overlook: do you not love that Allah should forgive you? Good women are for good men; those are declared innocent of what they say.

outline.title: The proprieties of a chaste society
outline.summary: O you who believe, do not enter houses other than your own until you have asked leave and greeted their people. Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their chastity; and tell the believing women to lower their gaze, guard their chastity, not display their adornment beyond what appears of it, and draw their head-coverings over their chests. Marry the single among you. Let those who cannot find the means to marry keep chaste until Allah enriches them. Do not force your slave-girls into prostitution.

outline.title: The Light, and the darknesses
outline.summary: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The likeness of His light is a niche in which is a lamp; the lamp in a glass; the glass like a brilliant star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow though no fire touched it: light upon light (24:35). In houses Allah has permitted to be raised, men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from His remembrance. But the deeds of those who disbelieve are like a mirage in a plain — or like darknesses in a deep sea, wave upon wave, cloud above: he to whom Allah gives no light has no light.

outline.title: “We hear and we obey”
outline.summary: They say, “We believe in Allah and the Messenger, and we obey”; then a party of them turns away. When they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, some refuse — but if the right is theirs, they come to him readily. The only saying of the believers is: “We hear and we obey.” Allah has promised those of you who believe and do right that He will make them successors in the land, establish for them their religion, and give them security in place of their fear.

outline.title: Within the house, and with the Messenger
outline.summary: Let your servants and your children who have not reached maturity ask leave of you at three times: before the dawn prayer, when you lay aside your garments at noon, and after the night prayer. There is no blame on the blind, the lame or the sick, nor on you, in eating at the houses of your kin; and when you enter houses, greet one another with a greeting from Allah. The believers do not leave a common matter without asking the Messenger’s leave. Do not make his summons among you like your calling one another. Let those who go against his command beware.

keyAyah.why: The ayah that gives the surah its name. Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and Ibn ʿAbbās understood the likeness as that of His light in the heart of the believer.

virtues.text: ʿĀʾishah said: “May Allah have mercy on the first emigrant women. When Allah sent down ‘and let them draw their head-coverings over their chests,’ they tore their wraps and covered themselves with them.”

before: Al-Muʾminūn named, among the marks of the successful, “those who guard their chastity.” Al-Nūr opens with the law for those who do not, and for those who accuse the innocent.
after: Al-Nūr ends: “He knows what you are upon.” Al-Furqān opens by blessing the One who sent down the Criterion, that it might be a warning to the worlds.
